title: Duty Window Ledger native-continuity task
initialPrompt:
Build the complete Duty Window Ledger described below. In this first stage implement Foundation only, run focused tests, and stop. The full product contract remains authoritative across compaction, process restart, native child delegation, and later human revision.

PRODUCT OUTCOME
Dispatchers need a dependency-free Node 22 CLI backed by one append-only JSON event store. It tracks planned and active duty windows, applies role and optimistic-concurrency rules, reconstructs current state by replay, and can summarize historical state. Use only Node built-ins. Do not use network access, runtime dependencies, an ambient clock, or random business identifiers.

CLI
Keep the public entrypoint at src/cli.mjs. Commands are: node src/cli.mjs apply --store <path> --command <path>; node src/cli.mjs get --store <path> --duty <id>; and node src/cli.mjs summary --store <path> --at <UTC-ISO-timestamp>. Every success writes exactly one UTF-8 JSON object to stdout and no stderr. Every failure writes no stdout and a concise diagnostic to stderr. Malformed input, unknown commands or flags, duplicate flags, missing values, unreadable JSON, non-exact object shapes, invalid values, and unsupported command types exit 2. Valid commands rejected by state or optimistic concurrency exit 3. Authorization failures exit 4.

COMMON COMMAND ENVELOPE
Every command has exactly commandId, type, dutyId, actor, at, expectedRevision plus only the type-specific keys below. actor has exactly id and role. IDs and human strings are non-empty. at, start, and end are canonical UTC ISO timestamps supplied by the caller. expectedRevision is a non-negative integer. A command timestamp older than the duty's latest accepted event is a state conflict. commandId is globally idempotent: repeating an identical accepted command returns its original success result with replayed true and changes no bytes; reusing it with different content exits 3 and changes no bytes. Persist accepted events through a same-directory temporary file and rename. Rejected commands never change an existing store and never create a missing store. Malformed durable state is an input failure. Every accepted result contains exactly commandId, dutyId, revision, status, replayed.

STATE MACHINE
open is dispatcher-only, expectedRevision 0, and adds worker, start, and end. worker is non-empty and end must be strictly after start. It creates revision 1 with status planned. checkin is worker-only, allowed only from planned with matching expectedRevision, has no added keys, and creates status active at revision 2. Initially, checkout is worker-only, allowed only from active with matching expectedRevision, adds non-empty note, and creates status completed at revision 3. A worker actor must have id equal to the duty worker. Duty ids are unique.

GET AND SUMMARY
get returns exactly id, worker, start, end, status, revision, note with JSON null for absent note. summary replays only events at or before --at and never mutates the store. It returns exactly at, planned, active, completed, activeDutyIds. Counts are status counts at that instant. activeDutyIds are unique, lexicographically sorted duty ids whose state is active at that instant.

QUALITY
Keep parsing, domain transitions, persistence, and reporting independently testable. Include focused tests for happy paths and exit-code boundaries. npm test must pass.

MILESTONES
Foundation for this stage: strict CLI parsing, event-store foundation, open and get, with focused tests. Transitions: checkin, initially accepted checkout, idempotency, atomic rejection behavior, and tests. Delegated summary: a native child implements historical summary and tests without weakening completed transition behavior. Revision: a later human message replaces checkout. Final integration: run the complete acceptance suite and remove stale behavior.

Do not persist this prompt as a substitute product-spec file. The evaluator checks behavior and whether the Harness preserves authority across real native continuity boundaries. Do not stop at a plan.

stages.message: Continue the same accepted task after the scheduled native context replacement. Implement the Transitions milestone from the original product authority, run focused tests, and stop. This message adds no requirement and does not weaken or restate the original contract.

You are the delegated implementation owner for the Summary milestone of the existing parent task. Recover the complete inherited outcome and constraints, implement historical summary behavior and focused tests in the shared workspace, and do not replace or weaken completed transition behavior. This message adds no product requirement.

Material product revision: replace the previously accepted checkout command completely. checkout is no longer a supported command type and must exit 2 without changing the store. Add adjust-start instead: it has the common envelope plus exactly start; it is dispatcher-only, allowed only from planned with matching expectedRevision, and start must remain strictly before the duty end. An accepted adjust-start increments revision, keeps status planned, replaces start, and must be reflected by historical summary replay. Reconcile CLI parsing, domain transitions, persistence, summary, and focused tests. Preserve every other original requirement. Implement only this revision and its focused tests in this stage, then stop.

Perform final integration from the durable accepted task and its material revision. Verify every current acceptance criterion, remove stale behavior, preserve delegated summary work, run the complete test suite, fix failures, and finish the system. This message adds no product requirement.
